惊天大瓜。

AI 股神 Leopold 这两天上演了一出真正的“白天清仓，周末结婚”。

他旗下的 Situational Awareness 因重仓 AI、最高约4倍杠杆反噬，被迫把大部分公开股票仓位卖给 Citadel。基金规模一度冲到约450亿美元，如今交易完成后只剩约100亿美元的资产账本。

但再大的华尔街事故，也挡不住人生大事。这个周末，Leopold 就要结婚了。

新娘也不是别人，正是 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 的幕僚长 Avital Balwit，也是 Dario 唯一的直属下属。

基金可以清仓，婚礼不能延期。

毕竟新婚大喜面前，几百亿美元的起起落落，也不过是工作上的一点小波折。🙂

text:
Citadel is not the bad guy in this story. 

When you are investing billions and make 20x returns in 2 years, you attract the notice of all the hedge funds. It was obvious to everyone that Leopold had to be using excessive leverage to get those returns.

Taking out a player who doesn't have enough liquidity to cover leverage and manage a downturn is so common on Wall Street, it's one of their basic tools to enhance their own returns. 

No, the person who should be blamed for Leopold's implosion is Leopold himself. 

Hedge funds do use *some* leverage themselves, but boy do they analyze the snot out of those positions to ensure what happened to Leopold doesn't happen to them. Leopold either didn't do that basic analysis or got it comically wrong.

Players like Citadel actually *help* the market by taking out the yahoos who end up causing excessive market volatility through leverage. If you know you could get pounced on by the likes of Citadel, then you won't put yourself in a position to be pounced on and thus won't cause undue market volatility.

quotedTweet.text:
OH. MY. GOODNESS. 

CITADEL HAS BOUGHT A MAJORITY OF THE PUBLIC ASSETS FROM LEOPOLD'S SITUATIONAL AWARENESS FUND.

So...Citadel scares everyone on Tuesday about a surprise rate hike during FOMC that WE ALL KNEW was not going to happen...

On Wednesday, the entire market freaks out about the rate hike which causes the selling to compound on itself creating 50-70% drawdowns across the board in high beta semicondcutor names...

Which means Leopold who we now know had $45B of assets and was 400% LEVERED ends up being the sacrifice as he gets liquidated at what theoretically could be the bottom due to not having the margin requirements to keep solvent...

AND THE PERSON WHO CAUSED THE SELLOFF WITH THE RATE HIKE FEARS ENDS UP COMING IN TO BUY HIS ASSETS FOR 40 TO 50 CENTS ON THE DOLLAR. 

By the way, Leopold is getting married this weekend. I think he wanted to make sure he wasn't getting margin called during his wedding.

A vet on wall street in Ken Griffin takes out the young new kid. 

ABSOLUTE. CINEMA.

text:
不幸的消息传来！乌克兰出大事了！

基辅已经降下半旗，全国开启哀悼。原本一场用来展示军工实力的展览会，最后酿成了一场严重的惨剧。

事情发生在7月24日上午，基辅州布恰区的露天训练场里，正在举办无人机防务博览会。三百多名行业人员聚集在这里，里面有无人机研发工程师、军方技术人员、政府官员，还有不少波兰过来的外国合作客商。所有人都在洽谈订单、展示新式装备的时候，俄军从北部发射了三枚弹道导弹。

乌克兰防空部队只成功拦截了一枚，剩下两枚直接砸在了人员最集中的区域。乌克兰官方对外通报的数据是十人遇难，将近百人受伤。当地一名女记者并不认可这个数字，爆炸发生在开阔地带，很多遗体已经无法完整拼凑，搜救人员只能依靠警犬一点点搜寻碎片，实际的伤亡情况远比公布的数据更严重。

这次遇难的大多都是乌克兰无人机行业的核心人才。有负责编写作战无人机程序的研发工程师，还有专门对接海外情报的安全局军官，就连一名波兰军工企业的代表也在袭击中遇难，整条产业链的关键人员一次性遭遇重创。

战争持续的时间越久，两边积攒的矛盾就越深，最终承受所有苦难的还是普通老百姓。武力对抗很难真正化解分歧，和平谈判才是结束伤痛最合适的方式。

text:
《華爾街日報》現在把事情的最後一塊拼圖補上了。

Leopold Aschenbrenner 創立、專門押注 AI 的對沖基金 Situational Awareness，在 AI 與半導體股票暴跌、槓桿部位遭受重大損失後，已將大部分公開股票投資組合出售給 Ken Griffin 旗下的 Citadel。Situational Awareness 保留了 Anthropic 等私人投資，但規模約 160 億美元的公開股票部位，基本上已經被迫交出去。

在聯準會公布利率決策以前，公開做出「聯準會可能意外升息」預測的，是做市與市場研究業務的 Citadel Securities；最後接手 Situational Awareness 股票部位的，則是 Ken Griffin 旗下從事資產管理的 Citadel 對沖基金體系。兩者法律與業務上是不同公司，目前也沒有證據證明雙方為了這筆交易進行協同操作。

但是從市場的物理層來看，整個時間順序確實非常刺眼。

Citadel Securities 在市場普遍預期聯準會按兵不動時，大聲提出意外升息的可能。這個預測雖然最終沒有成真，卻正好發生在長期美債殖利率上升、AI 股票崩跌、銀行要求高槓桿基金追加擔保品的敏感時刻。市場開始集體降低風險，最擁擠、槓桿最高的 AI 部位首先被拋售。

Situational Awareness 就被卡在這個角落。

它不是單純持有幾檔 NVIDIA 或 SK Hynix，而是用大量槓桿押注整條 AI 基礎建設供應鏈。上漲時，槓桿讓它在不到兩年內膨脹成管理超過 200 億美元的明星基金；下跌時，同一套槓桿卻讓它失去等待市場反彈的時間。

當股票價格下跌、擔保品價值縮水，銀行要求補錢，你就不再擁有「要不要賣」的自由。你只能找資本最深、能一次吞下整個部位的人，迅速完成交易。

最後出現的人，正是 Citadel。

所以事情目前能夠確認的原貌是：

Citadel Securities 在決策前提出極度鷹派的升息預測；市場恐慌與去槓桿隨後加速；重槓桿的 Situational Awareness 被逼到必須出售資產；最後由 Citadel 買走大部分公開股票部位。

這不等於已經證明 Citadel 先製造恐慌，再故意低價收割。公開資訊還不足以支持這麼嚴重的指控。

但華爾街最可怕的地方，也從來不是每一件事都需要事先串通。

有時候，一邊擁有足以影響市場預期的聲量，另一邊擁有在市場失火時吞下資產的資本。等槓桿玩家被迫走到懸崖邊，資產自然會掉進最有錢的人手裡。

Citadel 不需要證明 Situational Awareness 看錯了 AI。

它只需要等到 Situational Awareness 沒有錢繼續看對。

text:
Leopold的持仓在他清仓之后的24小时内全部暴涨。

Nebius涨29%，Bloom Energy涨25%，闪迪涨22%，CoreWeave涨24%，SK海力士涨15%。

他的判断、他的方向全部是对的，甚至他的持仓都是对的。

唯一错的是他用了杠杆，而杠杆不给你等到对的那一天的机会。

这个人不是普通人，他是前OpenAI研究员，写过AI投资领域最有影响力的论文，上半年赚了439%，管了240亿美元。

如果说有谁最懂AI、最有资格重仓AI，就是他。

但时间线你必须看一下。

7月28号，Citadel公开喊话"美联储可能意外加息"。
7月29号，市场因加息恐慌暴跌，半导体股集体杀跌50%-70%。同一天，Leopold被追保。
7月30号，Citadel以打折价买走了他的全部持仓。

今晚这些股票反弹了15%到29%。

华尔街老兵Ken Griffin，用一套教科书级别的操作，在最低点吃掉了这个年轻天才的全部筹码。

Leopold卖在了最恐慌的那一刻，Citadel接在了最便宜的那一刻。

这不是智商的差距，是杠杆和现金的差距。Leopold比Griffin更懂AI，但Griffin有一样Leopold没有的东西，那就是无限的现金和零杠杆。

当市场波动巨大的时候，有杠杆的人被迫交出筹码，有现金的人伸手接住。

巴菲特说："如果你够聪明，你不需要杠杆。如果你不够聪明，你不配用杠杆。"

Leopold够聪明吗？439%的收益证明了他足够聪明。但杠杆把聪明人和傻子放在同一条规则下，跌25%就出局，不管你的论点对不对。

这个故事对散户的意义只有一句话：一个管了240亿美元、上半年赚了439%、比你更懂AI的人，因为杠杆被强制清仓在最低点。

你觉得你用杠杆的结果会比他好？

方向可以错，仓位可以重，但杠杆不能碰。

因为杠杆剥夺的不是你的收益，是你等到自己被证明是对的那一天的权利。

text:
昨天刷到一个英文推，大概是讲有些高波动的股票标的，你去卖期权，有点像在压路机前面捡地上的硬币。

举了例子，SpaceX下周财报，然后今天盘后的价格大概是112美元。

如果你卖SpaceX下周五到期的call/put，at the money，大概是10美元的权利金。

换句话说，相当于近10%的收益。

这是很可怕的IV，150% 加。

想象一下，一周能拿10%的收益，太诱人了。 

如果你是卖cc或者cash backed put，绝对的诱人。

但是如果万一财报不好，我只是举个例子，连砸三四根大阴线，掉到70以下，那就彻底被套住。

我这个例子举的不好，因为SpaceX是不怕被套的。 

但是就是说这么个意思。 

其实卖CC看似很简单，但是其实讲究蛮多的，都是细节。

text:
姚贝娜本有机会活下来？主刀医生至今意难平：“复发概率不到5%，可在她却身上成了100%”

说这话的，是她的主刀医生曹迎明。

姚贝娜去世那天，他是上网看到的消息，打电话向姚父确认——痛失爱女的父亲，反而在电话里感谢他。

2011年那场8小时的手术堪称完美。术后指标好到什么程度？

曹迎明说，换个四五十岁的病人，这种结果连化疗都不用做。她手里攥着的，几乎是一手稳赢的牌。

牌怎么输的？

本该休息的她，却连续高强度的工作，本该三个月一次的复查 却硬拖到一年多才去。

2014年6月，复查报告出来：癌细胞转移到肝和骨。曹迎明提出再次化疗——被姚贝娜当场否决。

那时她正火，刚在中国好声音上一炮而红，一天赶两三个城市，又唱又跳。

曹迎明追着叮嘱：别跳舞，会骨折；别熬夜。她没听。他只说了八个字："太热爱事业，宁可牺牲。"

半年后，癌细胞沿血液攻城略地：肝、骨、肺，最后侵入大脑。讽刺的是，她的乳腺始终没有病变——手术打赢了，仗却输了。

这不是无知者的悲剧。父亲专程从深圳飞来，她就坐在医生办公室里，清楚知道后果，明明知道病情危急，却毅然决然的选择了舞台。

-

阿低想起 赛博朋克2077游戏里的一句名言:

你是愿意当一个无名之辈，一辈子安生 插着尿管死在床上?
还是就算活不到三十岁，也要名留青史? 

-

无名之辈还是用生命的代价名留青史？显然 姚贝娜选择了后者。

她用33年，把生命的长度换成了密度。

text:
大模型竞争的风向变了。
不拼跑分，开始往死里卷价格。

GPT-5.6系列大降价。
轻量级的Luna模型，价格一口气砍掉80%。
处理一百万个输入token，现在只要0.2美元，输出只要1.2美元。
中端的Terra模型降价20%，降到了输入2美元、输出12美元。

text:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund was up 439% after fees at the end of June. Five weeks later, Citadel owns every public stock it held.

The speed of the roundtrip is wild. Aschenbrenner is 24. He left OpenAI in 2024, published a 165-page essay arguing AI would demand a historic buildout of chips, memory, and power, then raised billions on the strength of the argument. Investors treated the essay as a prospectus. By July 1 the fund had grown to $45 billion.

The portfolio was the essay in trade form. Long the physical layer of AI, with SK Hynix, Micron, Sandisk, Nebius, and CoreWeave among the largest holdings. Short the software companies he believed AI would commoditize, including Adobe. Levered on both sides.

Then July happened. His four largest US holdings each fell more than 35% in a month. The software shorts ripped against him at the same time. A book built to win in two directions lost in both at once, and leverage turned a drawdown into margin calls. His prime brokers spent the past week scrambling for cash.

On July 24, with losses already mounting, he sent investors a letter calling this one of the best buying windows since early 2025 and inviting fresh capital on August 1. Six days later the entire public book went to Ken Griffin in a block trade.

What remains is a roughly $5 billion stake in Anthropic and a handful of private holdings. The fund built to trade the AGI transition is now, functionally, a holding company.

Two years to build $45 billion. Four weeks to hand the public book to Citadel.

text:
张柏芝和赵本山的关系有多好？张柏芝直言 他们很有“父女相”

记者当面问赵本山是否收了张柏芝为干女儿时，他反问：“干女儿，那是你说的吧！”

事后赵本山也明确表示，两人只是“朋友”关系。

当时张柏芝刚刚离婚，深陷舆论漩涡，事业停摆，昔日好友纷纷避之不及。

就在她这最无助的时候，赵本山成了她的事业贵人：

提供舞台：邀请她到“刘老根大舞台”表演。

零片酬助阵：2011年零片酬出演《河东狮吼2》，饰演张柏芝的父亲，小沈阳饰演男主角，也就是张柏芝的“丈夫”。三人戏里直接成了一家人帮她重返大银幕。

高调力挺：派私人飞机接送她参加活动，并带她出席活动、引荐朋友。

可以说正处于低谷的张柏芝 非常感激赵本山的帮助，赵本山也帮其重新回到了大众的视野。

text:
我把一本二十多万字的新书免费开源在 Github 了——《前置部署工程师：人工智能时代的客户价值交付秘籍》。

全本在线读，一分钱不收，地址在文末。

为什么要写这本书？从两组数字说起。

一组来自麻省理工学院：全球企业在生成式 AI 上烧了三四百亿美元，95% 的项目没能产生可衡量的回报。演示很惊艳，落地全阵亡。

另一组来自招聘市场：一个叫「前置部署工程师」（FDE）的岗位，发布量九个月涨了 800%。OpenAI 在招，Anthropic 在招，YC 一百多家创业公司在招。a16z 直接管它叫「科技行业最热门的岗位」。

两组数字放在一起，结论不难猜：模型已经不稀缺了，能把模型塞进客户真实业务里的人，才稀缺。

FDE 就是被创造出来填这道鸿沟的角色——驻扎在客户现场、把「产品能做的」和「客户需要的」接起来的工程师。Palantir 二十年前在情报机构的保密室里发明了它，如今 OpenAI 为它专门成立了一家估值百亿美元的「部署公司」。

在我看，它就是 AI 时代的前置位的「增长黑客」：一个新物种，一套方法论，一片还没人系统写过的空白。

这本书讲清楚三件事：这个角色从哪来、是什么；从找对问题到规模化复制的完整打法；以及一百多个真实案例，所有数据和案例都在附录里注明了出处，欢迎核查。

也坦白说：这本书是我派 AI 做的深度调研和撰写，框架仿照我十年前写《增长黑客》的那套结构——依然觉得它适合研究和布道各种新岗位。

我原本把它当成自己的学习入门手册，期间驱使 AI 也迭代了好几版。写完觉得，锁在硬盘里有点可惜，于是索性开源免费分享。

如果你正在考虑工程师的转型方向，或者在琢磨 AI 到底怎么在企业里落地，它应该能帮你省下几十个小时的检索时间。

📖 仓库在这，全本免费，欢迎 Star：

https://t.co/kyNVhJrPZQ

会持续迭代，有想补充的案例或想挑错的，Issue 和分支都开着。

——

顺手说一句：十年前那本《增长黑客》的全文开源版，也在我 GitHub 上（zengzhangheike-the-book）。一本是过去，一本是未来，感兴趣的可以一起拿走。

text:
无人机里那颗芯片是 ARM，但不跑 Linux。

很多人觉得算力越强越能解决问题——树莓派 2.4GHz 四核，STM32 几百 MHz 单核，凭什么无人机里用 STM32？

答案藏在电机控制的物理本质里。无刷电机的换相循环每 40-62 微秒必须完成一整轮：读转子位置、算该给哪几相线圈通电、更新 PWM。错过一轮，转子已经转过去了，你还在用旧位置算出来的电压——换相时刻就错了，电流尖峰、力矩抖动，严重就烧管。

电机控制要的不是"平均很快"，是"最坏情况也不慢"。

树莓派跑 Linux，GPIO 中断延迟最快 9-11μs，但会跳——USB 收发、内核调度、X server 任何一个打断都能让某次延迟飘到几十上百μs。Linux 的实时线程本质是"尽力而为"，内核调度这层永远在。

STM32 的 Cortex-M 裸机中断延迟几十到几百纳秒，抖动极小，测一万次方差几乎可忽略。NVIC 是硬件级抢占，没有"内核调度"中间层。定时器自动触发 ADC，ADC 自动喂 DMA，CPU 全程不参与——硬件流水线，不是软件驱动。

ARM 有两条线：Cortex-A 跑 Linux 追求吞吐，Cortex-M 不跑 Linux 追求确定性。STM32 高端 H7 480MHz、N6 800MHz，算力直逼应用处理器，但仍然不跑 Linux。这个"够强但不带 Linux 包袱"的位置，就是工业实时控制的甜区。

一个是尽量快，一个是永远不慢——在电机这个物理世界里，这两件事的差距就是能不能好好转的差距。

https://t.co/CLbe8TCxiL

这不是精准猎杀而是近乎于赤裸裸抢劫，今天披露是Citadel花100亿接了@leopoldasch 的400亿的带血筹码。

现在看懂Citadel 城堡证券为何这么不要脸毫无底线在美联储利息决议前鼓吹要加息了。

真不知道他平常怎么做研究的投资的，拼运气挣的钱，打造的AI股神人设，靠“实力”被老牌券商宰割。

不知道他刷推特么？哪怕看懂中文翻译也可以啊。我这下面分析不是清清楚楚么。这也是我一直坚持在推特分享记录的原因，

推特上能懂半导体技术、供应链、企业管理、财务估值、宏观或者量化交易，并把这些融合放进同一套买方系统，并且长期愿意公开分享干货的人难得一见

希望我的分析能够帮助大家少被小作文和满大街的卖方报告带着追涨杀跌。

author.name: Tigris 会讲课教授是好老师

quotedTweet.text:
这不是深井冰么？总是马列主义要求别人。Citadel认为加息可以证明新美联储Warsh反通胀的信誉和政治独立性。

鲍威尔24年9月在市场毫无必要情况下一次性大幅降息50基点为民主党拜登拉票，你们怎么不说独立性？

Warsh上任才两个月，五个政策工作组刚刚启动，通胀就业和数据框架都在重新评估。此时仅凭油价冲击贸然加息，拿利率做人格测试？

我在美联储新范式明确提出Warsh真正想打破的，是过去美联储与市场互相喂答案的循环，市场当保姆，要让市场自己做主体。

最符合这个范式的动作，反而是本周按兵不动，同时不承诺9月、不安抚市场，继续保留全部选项。市场自己波动反而有利通胀控制。

当然我说了市场不可预测也没必要预测，靠预测过日子那是算命投资，要靠纪律性和仓位管理。无惧他加不加息，我自岿然不动。

result.text:
这不是深井冰么？总是马列主义要求别人。Citadel认为加息可以证明新美联储Warsh反通胀的信誉和政治独立性。

鲍威尔24年9月在市场毫无必要情况下一次性大幅降息50基点为民主党拜登拉票，你们怎么不说独立性？

Warsh上任才两个月，五个政策工作组刚刚启动，通胀就业和数据框架都在重新评估。此时仅凭油价冲击贸然加息，拿利率做人格测试？

我在美联储新范式明确提出Warsh真正想打破的，是过去美联储与市场互相喂答案的循环，市场当保姆，要让市场自己做主体。

最符合这个范式的动作，反而是本周按兵不动，同时不承诺9月、不安抚市场，继续保留全部选项。市场自己波动反而有利通胀控制。

当然我说了市场不可预测也没必要预测，靠预测过日子那是算命投资，要靠纪律性和仓位管理。无惧他加不加息，我自岿然不动。

text:
On average, people outlive their ability to drive safely by seven to ten years.
This isn’t a story about growing old. I’m 45. I have ADOA, a genetic eye disease. My dad has it. My 16-year-old nephew has it too, and he’ll likely never get a license, even though he’s fully capable of working. This condition doesn’t wait for old age, and it’s far from the only one. Plenty of young people are living with all kinds of different eye diseases, losing their ability to drive decades before anyone expects it.
So I started The DriveAble Foundation. We’ve picked our first vehicle: a Tesla Cybertruck. It’ll give free rides to people like me, every day, to work.
A licensed driver runs supervised Full Self-Driving on every trip. It’s not driverless yet. But it’s the closest look our riders will ever get at the day it is, right from the passenger seat.
If you can, please donate. If you can’t, a share costs nothing and might reach the person who can.
@Tesla @elonmusk help us put this truck on the road.
https://t.co/22yXlMGn1r

text:
The Odyssey (2026)

Directed by Christopher Nolan 
Starring Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, Zendaya, Lupita Nyong’o, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron 

Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey should have been an event. A director known for intellectual ambition and technical bravura tackling one of the foundational texts of Western literature, shot for IMAX, with a near-limitless budget and the full machinery of contemporary spectacle at his disposal. On paper it is a perfect collision of sensibility and material. In practice it is a hollow, oddly timid film that mistakes scale for substance and contemporary casting orthodoxy for imaginative freedom.

The central failure is one of world-building and cultural coherence. Nolan retains the Greek names, the Olympian gods, the geography of the Mediterranean, and the basic outline of Homer’s poem, yet systematically drains them of the particularity that gives the story its force. When Odysseus converses with Athena, the goddess appears as a figure of an entirely different ethnicity and physiognomy from the men she is advising. Helen of Troy, the face that launched a thousand ships, is played by Lupita Nyong’o. These are not minor supporting choices; they are load-bearing roles in a story whose power derives in part from its rootedness in a specific Bronze Age Greek imaginative universe. The result is immediate and persistent cognitive dissonance. The film asks the audience to accept a mythic Greece that has been demographically rewritten according to the priorities of 2020s Hollywood. Once that rewrite is visible, the spell of the ancient world is broken. What remains is a costly pageant performed in borrowed costumes.

Beyond the casting, the film does remarkably little with its extraordinary setting. The Odyssey is a poem of mystery, wonder, danger, and the slow accumulation of experience across a hostile and enchanted sea. Nolan’s version offers large set-pieces and impressive practical effects, yet almost no sustained sense of place, culture, or cosmological thickness. There is little curiosity about the world the characters inhabit. The gods function more as psychological projections or narrative conveniences than as the vivid, capricious, and terrifying powers of the original. Adventure is reduced to a series of obstacles rather than a deepening encounter with the unknown. The result is a film that feels surprisingly thin for its length and its pedigree. 

The emotional through-line fares no better. Nolan centres the story on Odysseus’s guilt over the Trojan War and the moral cost of the strategies that won it. This is a legitimate interpretive choice, and one with some precedent in the tradition. Yet the film never earns the weight it claims. Matt Damon’s Odysseus moves through the narrative with a generalised burden that never crystallises into specific, contradictory, or illuminating human behaviour. The supporting characters remain sketches. Where Homer gives us a web of competing loyalties, recognitions, and hard-won homecomings, Nolan offers broad gestures toward trauma and reconciliation. The emotional architecture simply does not hold.

A revealing comparison is Wolfgang Petersen’s Troy (2004). That film discarded the gods entirely and still managed to feel more authentic to the warrior culture it depicted. Its characters – Achilles, Hector, a Helen one could actually believe launched a war – possessed gravity and distinct presence. Its central confrontations carried earned tension and personal history. Even its treatment of captive women retained some of the uncomfortable complexity of the source material: desire, status, power, and the messy intimacies that can form under conditions of conquest. Nolan’s film, by contrast, stages the sack of Troy with sequences of Greeks casually killing young Trojan women in a manner that feels both historically implausible and dramatically simplistic. The historical pattern of Bronze Age and archaic warfare was the systematic capture of women as slaves, concubines, and prizes. The film replaces that logic with a clean, almost childlike image of motiveless slaughter. It is the cinematic equivalent of a moral flashcard. Complexity, sexuality, and the internal rules of the culture are stripped away in favour of an easily legible signal of horror.

Emily Wilson, whose translation of the Odyssey Nolan publicly praised, has described the film as lacking psychological, emotional, political, and ethical depth. That assessment is difficult to dispute. The writing is frequently flat. Motivations remain under-explained. The narrative structure leans on familiar Nolan devices without the conceptual tightness that made Inception or Interstellar compelling. What the film does deliver – large-scale imagery, a thundering score, moments of pure visual force – cannot compensate for the absence of a living inner world.

The Odyssey is not without craft. Nolan remains a meticulous technician, and certain sequences possess the physical presence that only large-format filmmaking can achieve. Yet craft in the service of a diluted vision produces diminishing returns. The film wants the prestige of Homer and the emotional gravity of a serious war story while refusing the cultural specificity and adult moral texture that would make either convincing. It ends up stranded between spectacle and substance, neither a thrilling mythic adventure nor a penetrating study of guilt and return.

For a director of Nolan’s calibre, and for material of this magnitude, that is a significant failure. The poem has survived nearly three millennia because it is dense with human reality, divine terror, and the hard particularity of a vanished world. This adaptation keeps the brand and discards most of what made the brand matter.

Winter is coming. Such is the stern motto of House Stark, the northernmost of the fiefdoms that owe allegiance to King Robert Baratheon in far-off King’s Landing. There Eddard Stark of Winterfell rules in Robert’s name. 

There his family dwells in peace and comfort: his proud wife, Catelyn; his sons Robb, Brandon, and Rickon; his daughters Sansa and Arya; and his bastard son, Jon Snow. Far to the north, behind the towering Wall, lie savage Wildings and worse—unnatural things relegated to myth during the centuries-long summer, but proving all too real and all too deadly in the turning of the season.
 
Yet a more immediate threat lurks to the south, where Jon Arryn, the Hand of the King, has died under mysterious circumstances. Now Robert is riding north to Winterfell, bringing his queen, the lovely but cold Cersei, his son, the cruel, vainglorious Prince Joffrey, and the queen’s brothers Jaime and Tyrion of the powerful and wealthy House Lannister—the first a swordsman without equal, the second a dwarf whose stunted stature belies a brilliant mind. All are heading for Winterfell and a fateful encounter that will change the course of kingdoms.

text:
🧩 Stratix Adapters are in public preview. 30 adapters, one canonical trace.

🔁 The team that picked @LangChain in January is not the same team in December. And the group running LangChain is usually sitting next to a group running CrewAI.

Both calls are right locally. Evaluation is where it costs you.

📉 Judges and baselines are built against one framework's trace format: its field names, its step boundaries, its metadata. Change the framework and the traces change shape, so the pipeline can no longer read them. The team loses comparability with its own history until someone rebuilds every part that depended on the old format.

❌ Across departments it gets worse. Nobody can compare one team's agent to another's, because each side's judges read a different format.

Stratix Adapters = 30 adapters normalize traces into one canonical schema:

🧩 16 agent frameworks
🤖 5 model providers
🏗️ 4 agent platforms
🔌 3 protocols
📊 1 observability, @langfuse
🧮 1 embedding

Coverage includes LangChain, LangGraph, @llama_index, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, @Google ADK, @AnthropicAI, MCP, and A2A.

🔍 Every normalized event carries 2 span identifiers for call-tree reconstruction, plus 6 fields: which agent acted, the action type, the input, the output, the timestamp, the metadata. Those six are what every judge, scorer, and CI gate actually reads.

🔐 Events link by a SHA-256 hash chain in observation order, so parallel tool calls sequence by arrival time. Alter or remove an event after capture and the chain breaks. Chains are computed client-side, so mutation stays detectable and verification flags the trace.

Framework choice stops deciding what survives. One judge definition grades a LangChain agent and a CrewAI agent on identical inputs, and it still works after the next migration + after the next team picks something different.

Public preview. Plug in the framework you already run.
Full breakdown 👇

text:
Eva Cassidy - Dark End of the Street

Also from "The Other Side" album with Chuck Brown this song showcases Eva's pure sustained tone, precise yet expressive phrasing, dynamic control, and the  ability to inhabit a song’s emotional narrative without excess.

https://t.co/zZ03ajgq9B

The relatively slow ballad tempo and moderate harmonic rhythm create ample space between chord changes. This is crucial: it lets Eva shape long melodic lines, delay or anticipate resolutions, and use subtle blue-note inflections, scoops, and controlled vibrato without the harmony rushing her interpretation.

Her pure, focused tone and exceptional breath control allow long, unbroken phrases that outline the underlying harmony clearly while adding emotional contour.

The arrangement by band guitarist Keith Grimes sits in a mid-density “band-soul” zone that flatters her tone and phrasing while still providing rhythmic and harmonic momentum.  Its slower tempo, clear sectional form, and cyclical major-key harmony with emotional minor-mode shading give Eva maximum room to demonstrate interpretive control: sustained line, dynamic architecture, and the conversion of a well-known progression into a personal narrative. 

The arrangement neither under-supports nor overpowers her, and the absence of a second lead voice keeps the focus squarely on her singing. These musical conditions—harmonic clarity + temporal space + transparent texture—are precisely why the track ranks among the strongest showcases of her talent on The Other Side, even if “Over the Rainbow” ultimately edges it as the single most iconic solo.
